items.label: Iran/Hormuz conflict -- no ceasefire, Trump floats talks, Brent above $100/bbl
items.detail: Continued escalation with no resolution (live web search, Sept 9-10 sources): Iran's IRGC struck Jordan's Al-Azraq air base again on Sept 9 (Jordan intercepted 18 of 20 missiles, 2 fell in unpopulated areas) -- the base has now been targeted 10+ times since March 2026 (Al Jazeera, Sept 9-10). Trump said Sept 9 the renewed fighting "will not last long" and floated possible talks, with the war seen ending only "after election" (Al Jazeera liveblog, Sept 9). Qatar separately warned of an "industrial catastrophe" if the crisis continues (Al Jazeera, Sept 8). Brent crude is now quoted in a $101-105/bbl range depending on source/time-of-day (Trading Economics: $101.25 as of Sept 10; Fortune: ~$105.20 intraday Sept 10, roughly $3.15 above the prior morning) -- both above the $100 threshold crossed for the first time yesterday. Broader market fell in sympathy Sept 9 (S&P 500 -0.58%, Nasdaq 100 near -1%), with GOOG (-3.18% Sept 9, -2.31% more Sept 10-adjacent per timothysykes.com) hit by both the oil/rate backdrop and a youth-addiction-lawsuit overhang (appeals court cleared 2,400-3,000+ suits vs. Alphabet/Meta/Snap/TikTok) despite a fresh $15B EU AI-infrastructure announcement the same day. The account holds no direct oil & gas exposure but remains 69.60% concentrated in SPY5+SPYL, and GOOG (part of the AI/tech capex cluster) carries this litigation-specific overhang on top of the macro one.
items.recommendation: Do not add to SPY5/SPYL or initiate new discretionary equity purchases while the Iran/Hormuz conflict remains unresolved. Prioritize the DBC diversification action above (the one true negative-correlation hedge found this run) given continued oil/inflation-driven stress with Brent now durably above $100/bbl. Separately, watch GOOG's litigation exposure independent of the macro picture -- it is not yet large enough (part of a 5.12%-of-NAV cluster) to warrant a standalone trim, but do not add to the position while the appeals-court ruling is fresh.
